whatWeDo.title: What We Do
whatWeDo.subtitle: Not just engineers. Design, art, engineering, QA, and release under one roof, built to ship ambitious games across platforms.

engineering.title: Engineering
engineering.body: We work hands-on with Unreal, Unity, and Godot, and are comfortable with proprietary engines built in C/C++ and Rust. We focus on clean, stable systems and performance that holds up in production.

porting.title: Porting
porting.body: We ship to Xbox One, Xbox Series X|S, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2, and VR platforms like Meta Quest. We handle platform specifics carefully so gameplay, performance, and certification stay on track.

art.title: Art
art.body: Our artists work shoulder to shoulder with engineering: 3D, technical art, and in-engine integration. Assets look right and run right on every platform.

design.title: Game Design
design.body: Game and narrative design: mechanics, systems, balance, story, and dialogue. We design alongside your team, or shape a concept into something playable.

qa.title: QA and Release
qa.body: Our in-house QA team sits with engineering, tests changes fast, and runs platform compliance checks on every build. Then we take care of release: we set up titles on each platform and move builds through the full pipeline to production. Structured, repeatable, predictable.

backend.title: Backend and Cloud
backend.body: We build APIs and backend services on AWS, Azure, and Vercel using modern, production-ready stacks. Reliability, observability, and maintainability guide how we ship and operate.

ai.title: AI
ai.body: We develop and train in-house models that support teams at every stage of development, from prototyping to polish. The goal is to make real work faster, not to chase hype.

fullGames.title: Full Games
fullGames.body: A whole game from first concept to release: design, art, engineering, QA, and launch from one team. We have done it for a client and for a game of our own.

projects.title: Our Work
projects.subtitle: Proud to be part of these amazing projects.

privacy.title: Telemetry, analytics, and player data practices for our games.

events.body: Jams, meetups, anything about games. Tell us what you need.

plana.name: Plan A Collective
plana.body: Friends first, and close collaborators on the projects we share. Plan A brings the art: characters, environments, animation and VFX, and we join forces whenever a game needs both studios.

zet.name: Zet Labs
zet.body: Our sister company, building AI agents for teams. Together we train custom models for our game development needs and run them on our own hardware, so the tools fit the way we make games.

aiPolicy.title: AI where it matters. Creativity first.
aiPolicy.subtitle: AI is here, and we use it every day. But games are made by people, and that part is not up for automation.

switch.label: AI on your project
switch.onTitle: We use it where it matters.
switch.onBody: In code, AI assists and an engineer reviews every line. In production it takes on planning, pipelines, documentation and handoffs, so information stays current, easy to find, and inside the team.
switch.offBody: Not the right fit for your game? We switch it off, coding assistants included, and build it the way we always have: by hand. Same team, same standards.

creative.title: Creativity first. Always.
creative.body: Games are creative work and an art form. Design, art, story, and feel come from people, and no model replaces that here. Not now, not later.

code.title: In code, engineers stay in charge.
code.body: AI helps us write and check code faster. Every change is still read, tested and owned by an engineer, and held to the same standard as code written by hand. On your project it follows your rules: your tools, your policy, or none at all.

care.title: Deliberate, not default.
care.body: Every use of AI is a decision, not a habit. If it doesn't make the work better or the team faster, we don't use it.
care.note: It's the greener way, too: no compute and no energy spent where AI isn't needed.

local.title: Our models. Our hardware.
local.body: We train our own models and run them on our own inference hardware, fully offline. Nothing goes out to the cloud: your code and assets never leave machines we own.

howWeWork.title: How We Work
howWeWork.subtitle: Four ways to work with us. One goal: it should feel like one team.

embedded.label: Embedded
embedded.title: You drive.
embedded.body: Our engineers join your team: your stand-ups, your backlog, your direction. You point, we build.

scoped.label: Owned scope
scoped.title: Hand it over.
scoped.body: Give us a piece of the project: a port, a system, a platform. We plan it, build it, and bring it back finished.

mixed.label: Mixed
mixed.title: Both at once.
mixed.body: Engineers embedded in your day-to-day, plus a dedicated crew on the part you'd rather not think about.

full.label: Full game
full.title: The whole game.
full.body: Bring us a brief. We take the game from concept to release: design, art, code, QA, and launch.

team.title: No distance.
team.body: Our goal is to feel like your team, not a vendor. Same channels, same reviews, same standards. No layer in between.

tools.title: Your tools. Our backup.
tools.body: We work in your stack and your pipeline. Need more muscle? Plug into our in-house infrastructure, tuned for heavy workloads and massive data.

jobs.title: Join the Team

subtitle.intro: We work on games you might already have in your library: Beat Saber, Darkest Dungeon, and other titles on Steam and consoles. Our team of 30+ in Prague tackles hard technical problems and ships quality work for studios worldwide.
subtitle.culture: No crunch culture, no endless meetings. Just solid engineering, real ownership, and projects worth talking about. If that sounds like your kind of place, keep reading.

jobs.status: We're actively growing the team. See yourself in any of these? Say hi.

hiringProcess.title: Your Way In
hiringProcess.description: Short, simple, no pressure. Here's how it usually goes.
hiringProcess.note: We keep it flexible, so steps can vary by role.

steps.title: Email Marty
steps.description: Send as much as you can: CV, GitHub, portfolio, anything that shows how you think.

steps.title: We get back to you
steps.description: If it looks like a fit, you'll hear from us.

steps.title: Small task
steps.description: A simple task. Not a trivia test, just a way to see how you approach a problem.

steps.title: Review
steps.description: We review what you sent and talk it through with you.

steps.title: First interview
steps.description: You'll meet our team leads and HR at our HQ in Prague. We'll talk about your experience, how you work, and what the role looks like day to day.

steps.title: Second round
steps.description: A shorter conversation with our founder, usually more about culture fit, motivation, and whether it works for both sides.

steps.title: If it clicks
steps.description: If it's a mutual yes, welcome aboard.

contact.title: Don't See Your Role?
contact.description: We're always looking for talented people. Send us your CV and tell us what you're passionate about.

unrealEngineer.title: Unreal Engineer
unrealEngineer.description: Work on AAA titles using Unreal Engine. You'll tackle gameplay systems, optimize performance, and help ship to PC and consoles. Experience with Blueprints and C++ is required. You'll collaborate directly with partner studios on projects that millions of players will enjoy.

unityEngineer.title: Unity Engineer
unityEngineer.description: Build and ship games across multiple platforms using Unity. From mobile to console ports, you'll work on diverse projects that call for strong C# skills and a solid understanding of Unity's rendering and physics systems. Experience with platform-specific optimization is a plus.

cppMediorEngineer.title: C/C++ Engineer
cppMediorEngineer.description: Work on game systems and performance in C/C++. You'll implement gameplay features, optimize code paths, and help ship titles on PC and consoles. Solid C/C++ skills and experience with game or real-time systems are required. A great step for engineers ready to own meaningful technical work.

cppRustEngineer.title: C/C++ or Rust Engineer
cppRustEngineer.description: Dive deep into engine-level work. You'll optimize rendering pipelines, implement low-level systems, and solve the hardest technical challenges in game development. Experience with proprietary engines, graphics APIs, or systems programming is required. This role is for engineers who love working close to the metal.

backendEngineer.title: Backend Engineer
backendEngineer.description: Build the services that power games. You'll work on APIs, game backends, and cloud infrastructure on AWS and Azure. We care about reliability, clean architecture, and systems that scale. If you like solving real problems without the enterprise bloat, this is your spot.

pythonProgrammer.title: Python Programmer (Tooling & Integrations)
pythonProgrammer.description: Build internal tools and pipeline integrations that speed up game development. You'll work on automation, data workflows, and DCC integrations, including Blender, Maya, Houdini, and Unreal Python tooling used by art and production teams. We need someone who can turn complex production requirements into reliable scripts and services.
points: Blender, Maya, or Houdini Python API experience

qaEngineer.title: QA Engineer
qaEngineer.description: Keep quality high across platforms. You'll work directly with engineers, catch issues early, run platform compliance checks, and help us ship builds that pass certification the first time. We value sharp eyes, clear bug reports, and people who understand both players and the tech.

mediorProducer.title: Producer
mediorProducer.description: Run production on co-dev, porting, and internal work, often several streams at once. You'll keep plans honest, partners informed, and engineering and QA unblocked, all the way through cert, storefront submissions, and post-launch updates. You're close enough to the tech to talk builds and constraints with engineers, and clear-headed enough to cut scope when the date is real. This is a mid-level role: you've shipped, you don't hide behind process, and people trust the schedule you keep.
points: Shipped at least one title or major milestone

marketingManager.title: Marketing Manager
marketingManager.description: Shape how Flying Rat Studio connects with the game development world. You'll craft our messaging, manage our social presence, coordinate with partner studios on announcements, and help grow our reputation as a go-to technical partner. Experience in games or B2B tech marketing is preferred.
points: 2+ years in B2B or games marketing

juniorIt.title: IT Specialist
juniorIt.description: Keep our team of 30+ running smoothly. You'll manage workstations, handle UniFi/Ubiquiti networking, support dev environments, and maintain our Dell EMC servers with VMware ESXi virtualization. We use Synology for storage and run various Linux distributions for VMs. A great opportunity to grow your IT skills in a fast-paced game development environment.

officeCultureManager.title: Office & Culture Manager
officeCultureManager.description: Keep our Prague HQ running smoothly and make it a great place to work. You'll handle day-to-day office admin, budgets, and vendor coordination, organize team events and internal activities, and support HR with onboarding, recruitment, and candidate communication. A role for someone who thrives on keeping things organized and people happy.

about.boilerplate: Flying Rat Studio is a Prague-based game development team specializing in gameplay systems, performance optimization, rendering pipelines, and porting to PlayStation, Xbox, Switch, and handhelds. The studio works hands-on with Unreal, Unity, and Godot, and is comfortable with proprietary engines built in C/C++ and Rust.
